name: St. Paul's priest's house, Clinton Street

grade.why: Known from maps or written records; no picture of it has been found.

documented_range.note: Standing on the night of the fire, which destroyed it (Andreas vol. 2, pp. 406, 712-718).

change_note: Built T-3831 (2026-11-28): drawn in the 1871 scene on the landmark_1871 archetype, in place of the generic context fill that stood on its lot.

placement.position_note: On the parish's ground at Clinton and Mather (Andreas vol. 2, p. 406); its place north of the church, fronting Clinton Street, is reconstructed. The footprint's origin is local E -246.1 N -1514.5.
placement.symbolic_location: Clinton Street north of St. Paul's Church.

footprint.note: Reconstructed: a frame house of the size its $3,000 cost bought.

fire.note: The priest's residence was lost with the church (Andreas vol. 2, p. 406; Sheahan and Upton: 'with A $3,000 residence').

blocks.name: the priest's house
blocks.note: A two-storey frame house with its gable to Clinton Street, the size a $3,000 house of 1868 bought (Andreas vol. 2, p. 406). No picture or plan of it is known: its form is reconstructed as the West Side's frame houses.

value.note: ST. PAUL'S PRIEST'S HOUSE, built by T-3831: the $3,000 residence beside the church (Andreas vol. 2, p. 406), reconstructed.

composition.note: ST. PAUL'S PRIEST'S HOUSE, built by T-3831: the $3,000 residence beside the church (Andreas vol. 2, p. 406), reconstructed.

wall_material.value: Painted clapboard on a frame, a shingle roof
wall_material.note: Reconstructed as the West Side's frame houses.

function.note: The priest's residence of St. Paul's (Andreas vol. 2, p. 406); Rev. John Kilkenny was pastor in 1870-71.

built.note: Built with the parish's buildings after its founding in 1868 (Andreas vol. 2, p. 406).

citations.citation: Andreas, A. T. History of Chicago: From the Earliest Period to the Present Time. Vol. 2, From 1857 until the Fire of 1871. Chicago: A. T. Andreas, 1885.
what_it_supplies: clock hours at named places along the fire's path, 8-9 October 1871
the south line of the South Division ruin (Harrison and Congress streets) and where the fire was stopped
that M. D. Ogden's house on the North Side escaped
the gale from the south-west and the rain about eleven o'clock Monday night
what_it_does_not_supply: a surveyed outline of the burnt district
an hour for most individual buildings, which are interpolated between its stated hours

citations.citation: Sheahan, James W., and George P. Upton. The Great Conflagration. Chicago: Its Past, Present and Future. Philadelphia: Union Publishing Co., 1871.
what_it_supplies: the authors' count of the people made homeless by the fire of October 1871: 98,860
what_it_does_not_supply: anything about the buildings of 1812 or 1835: the town those scenes show was gone long before 1871

research_note: ST. PAUL'S PRIEST'S HOUSE, built by T-3831 for the 1871 scene: 'the priest's residence $3,000' (Andreas vol. 2, p. 406), lost in the fire with the church. Where it stood on the parish's ground and how it looked are not recorded: it is set north of the church on Clinton Street and drawn as a two-storey frame house.
